mission.title: helm: Rollback a failed chart upgrade stuck in pending-upgrade state
mission.description: After an interrupted `helm upgrade`, further upgrades fail with `Error: UPGRADE FAILED: another operation (install/upgrade/rollback) is in progress` because the release is stuck in `pending-upgrade`. Rollback to the last deployed revision is needed to recover.

steps.title: Inspect release status and history
steps.description:
```bash
helm status myapp -n prod
helm history myapp -n prod
```

Revision with STATUS pending-upgrade blocks new operations; note the last revision with STATUS deployed.

steps.title: Confirm no helm process is still running
steps.description:
```bash
ps aux | grep '[h]elm upgrade'
kubectl get secret -n prod -l owner=helm,name=myapp
```

Release state is stored in `sh.helm.release.v1.myapp.vN` secrets. Do not edit while a live upgrade is running.

steps.title: Roll back to the last good revision
steps.description:
```bash
helm rollback myapp 3 -n prod --wait --timeout 5m
```

If rollback also fails with the same error, go to the next step.

steps.title: Mark the stuck revision as failed when rollback is blocked
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl get secret sh.helm.release.v1.myapp.v4 -n prod -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.status}'
kubectl label secret sh.helm.release.v1.myapp.v4 -n prod status=failed --overwrite
helm rollback myapp 3 -n prod --wait
```

steps.title: Verify workloads and retry upgrade
steps.description:
```bash
helm history myapp -n prod
kubectl rollout status deploy/myapp -n prod
helm upgrade myapp ./chart -n prod --atomic --timeout 5m
```

Use `--atomic` so future failed upgrades auto-rollback.

resolution.summary: The root cause is that Helm records the new revision as `pending-upgrade` before applying manifests; if the client is killed or times out, the status is never updated, so Helm refuses further operations. Rolling back creates a new revision from the last deployed one, and relabeling the stuck secret as failed unblocks it because Helm only locks on pending-* states.
codeSnippets:
helm history myapp -n prod
helm rollback myapp 3 -n prod --wait --timeout 5m

kubectl label secret sh.helm.release.v1.myapp.v4 -n prod status=failed --overwrite
helm rollback myapp 3 -n prod --wait

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with helm available or the issue environment reproducible.
